author: Rhian Lowndes
title: Locally-owned pharmacy stops stocking GLP-1 medications, calls out insurance practices - NewsBreak
text:
By Rhian Lowndes ,
1 hours ago
RADFORD, Va. ( WFXR ) – As of April 1, Radford Drug will no longer stock GLP-1 medications.
Operations Manager Zan Armentrout said as the prices of these drugs rise, insurance companies and pharmacy benefit managers (PBMs) will only reimburse the amount written in a prior-made contract.
“If I bought a drug that cost me $500, which is what a lot of brand-name drugs cost, the insurance company may only pay me $430 or $400, so now I’m filling a drug and footing $70, $100 towards the bill,” he said.
Armentrout said while a large chain pharmacy can afford the difference or has its own contracts, the practice puts a strain on small, independent pharmacies.
Local pharmacies face challenges with underpaid prescriptions The problem, he added, isn’t limited to GLP-1s. That’s just one drug he can remove from his stock because not many of his customers use them.
“This isn’t a choice I wanted to make,” he said. “It’s a choice I had to make so that we can continue to give personalized service for the customers who need it.”
Armentrout said Radford Drug will still help their customers sign up for a mail-order pharmacy and coordinate their prescriptions if they need a GLP-1.
